chunks: And Fadl narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Yahya al-Tamtam al-Salami, from Uthman al-Naww, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'This matter was initially with me; then Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, postponed it, and He will do in my progeny what He wills.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, honorific for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.)
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: Fadl ibn Shadhan, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the postponement of the Imamate to his progeny?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological principle of *al-amr* (divine authority) being initially vested in Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) before being deferred to his progeny, specifically the Twelfth Imam. It underscores the Divine Will (*mashallah*) governing the timing of the reappearance, a key concept in Shia eschatology regarding the occultation. The hadith serves to reassure believers that the delay is not a loss of authority but a deliberate divine decree ensuring the Imamate's continuity within the Prophet's lineage.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 418 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Muhammad bin Ismail from Muhammad bin Sinan from Abu Yahya Tamtaam Salmi from Uthman Nawa that he said:
I heard Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) say: “Initially this task was entrusted to me; but later on the Almighty Allah postponed it and kept it in my progeny.”
